title: Sattu Paratha
steps: Mix sattu with chopped onion, green chilli, ginger, coriander, ajwain, mustard oil, lemon juice and salt to make the filling.
Knead a soft wheat dough. Stuff portions with the sattu mixture, seal and roll into parathas.
Cook on a hot tawa with ghee till golden on both sides.
Serve hot with curd, pickle or chutney.

fullIngredients.name: Onion, green chilli, ginger, coriander, ajwain, mustard oil, lemon, salt

tipsList.title: Tip 1
tipsList.desc: Classic Bihari breakfast – protein-rich and cooling due to sattu.

tipsList.title: Tip 2
tipsList.desc: Mustard oil in the filling is essential for authentic flavour.

title: Chura Dahi (Dahi Chura)
steps: Wash and lightly soak the chura if needed. Drain.
Mix with thick curd and jaggery or sugar. Add sliced banana or mango in season.
Serve as a light, cooling breakfast – especially popular in summer and on Makar Sankranti.

fullIngredients.name: Jaggery or sugar, banana or mango (seasonal)

tipsList.title: Tip 1
tipsList.desc: Simple, probiotic Bihari breakfast – Katarni chura is prized when available.

tipsList.title: Tip 2
tipsList.desc: Refreshing and easy to digest.

title: Puri with Aloo Sabzi
steps: Knead a stiff dough for puris. Roll and deep-fry till puffed and golden.
Prepare a simple spiced potato sabzi with onion, tomato and ginger.
Serve hot puris with the sabzi, often accompanied by jalebi or a sweet on special days.

fullIngredients.name: Onion, tomato, green chilli, ginger, spices
Oil for deep frying, ghee or oil for sabzi

tipsList.title: Tip 1
tipsList.desc: Classic festive or Sunday breakfast across Bihar.

tipsList.title: Tip 2
tipsList.desc: Puris should be light and well-puffed.

title: Litti Chokha
steps: Prepare sattu stuffing with mustard oil, garlic, ginger, chilli, ajwain, lemon and salt. Stuff into wheat dough balls and seal.
Roast the littis over charcoal, cow-dung cakes, or bake till the crust is crisp and slightly charred.
For chokha: Roast brinjal, tomato and boil potato. Mash with onion, green chilli, mustard oil and salt.
Dip hot littis in ghee and serve with chokha.

fullIngredients.name: Sattu, mustard oil, garlic, ginger, green chilli, ajwain, lemon, salt
Onion, mustard oil, green chilli for chokha

tipsList.title: Tip 1
tipsList.desc: The iconic dish of Bihar – smoky, rustic and deeply satisfying.

tipsList.title: Tip 2
tipsList.desc: Traditional open-fire roasting gives the authentic flavour.

title: Dal Bhaat with Chana Dal & Sabzi
steps: Cook rice and a simple tempered chana dal with onion, tomato and spices.
Prepare a dry or gravy vegetable sabzi and a side of chokha.
Serve the classic Bihari thali of rice, dal, sabzi, chokha, papad, pickle and curd.

fullIngredients.name: Onion, tomato, green chilli, ginger-garlic, spices
Seasonal vegetable sabzi, chokha, papad, pickle, curd

tipsList.title: Tip 1
tipsList.desc: Everyday Bihari lunch – simple, balanced and comforting.

tipsList.title: Tip 2
tipsList.desc: Curd is almost always present on the plate.

title: Dal Bhaat with Mixed Dal & Sabzi
steps: Cook rice and a simple tempered mixed dal with onion, tomato and spices.
Prepare a dry or gravy vegetable sabzi and a side of chokha.
Serve the classic Bihari thali of rice, dal, sabzi, chokha, papad, pickle and curd.

fullIngredients.name: Onion, tomato, green chilli, ginger-garlic, spices
Seasonal vegetable sabzi, chokha, papad, pickle, curd

tipsList.title: Tip 1
tipsList.desc: Everyday Bihari lunch made with mixed lentils.

tipsList.title: Tip 2
tipsList.desc: Simple, balanced and nourishing.

title: Kadhi Bari
steps: Make soft besan dumplings (bari), deep-fry and set aside.
Prepare a yogurt-besan kadhi, tempered with spices and ginger. Add the fried bari and simmer.
Serve with steamed rice.

tipsList.title: Tip 1
tipsList.desc: Comforting Bihari kadhi with soft fried dumplings.

tipsList.title: Tip 2
tipsList.desc: A popular home-style dish.

title: Bihari Mutton Curry
steps: Marinate mutton with yogurt and spices. Sauté onion and ginger-garlic till golden.
Add the mutton and cook till tender in a rich, spiced gravy.
Serve with roti, litti or rice – often a celebratory dish.

fullIngredients.name: Garam masala, red chilli, turmeric, oil

tipsList.title: Tip 1
tipsList.desc: Non-vegetarian food is typically reserved for special occasions in many Bihari homes.

tipsList.title: Tip 2
tipsList.desc: Slow cooking yields the best results.

title: Bihari Fish Curry
steps: Lightly fry fish pieces in mustard oil. Prepare a gravy with onion, tomato, ginger-garlic and spices.
Add the fish and simmer gently.
Serve with rice.

tipsList.title: Tip 1
tipsList.desc: Common in riverine and Mithila regions of Bihar.

tipsList.title: Tip 2
tipsList.desc: Mustard oil is the preferred cooking medium.

title: Bihari Fish Curry with Mustard (Angika Style)
steps: Lightly fry fish pieces in mustard oil. Prepare a gravy with onion, tomato, ginger-garlic and spices.
Add mustard paste and the fish. Simmer gently.
Serve with rice.

fullIngredients.name: Mustard oil, onion, tomato, ginger-garlic, mustard paste

tipsList.title: Tip 1
tipsList.desc: Angika-style fish curry with mustard paste for extra pungency.

tipsList.title: Tip 2
tipsList.desc: Common in the Mithila and Angika regions of Bihar.

title: Thekua
steps: Melt jaggery with a little water. Mix into wheat flour with ghee and cardamom to form a stiff dough.
Shape into small discs or use traditional moulds. Deep-fry on medium heat till golden and crisp.
Cool and store. Especially made for Chhath Puja.

fullIngredients.name: Oil or ghee for deep frying

tipsList.title: Tip 1
tipsList.desc: Iconic Chhath festival sweet of Bihar – crisp, mildly sweet and long-lasting.

tipsList.title: Tip 2
tipsList.desc: Ghee in the dough improves flavour and texture.

title: Ghugni with White Peas
steps: Pressure-cook the soaked white peas till soft. Prepare a spicy onion-tomato gravy with mustard oil.
Add the peas and simmer. Garnish with onion, green chilli, coriander and lemon.
Serve hot as a snack or with muri (puffed rice).

fullIngredients.name: Onion, tomato, ginger, green chilli, spices
Mustard oil, lemon, coriander for garnish

tipsList.title: Tip 1
tipsList.desc: Popular street and home snack made with white peas.

tipsList.title: Tip 2
tipsList.desc: Often eaten with puffed rice (ghugni-muri) in the Anga region.

title: Ghugni with Black Chickpeas
steps: Pressure-cook the soaked black chickpeas till soft. Prepare a spicy onion-tomato gravy with mustard oil.
Add the chickpeas and simmer. Garnish with onion, green chilli, coriander and lemon.
Serve hot as a snack or with muri (puffed rice).

fullIngredients.name: Onion, tomato, ginger, green chilli, spices
Mustard oil, lemon, coriander for garnish

tipsList.title: Tip 1
tipsList.desc: Popular street and home snack made with black chickpeas.

tipsList.title: Tip 2
tipsList.desc: Often eaten with puffed rice (ghugni-muri) in the Anga region.

title: Dal Pitha
steps: Cook and grind spiced chana dal into a filling. Make a soft rice-flour dough.
Stuff portions of dough with the dal mixture, shape into parcels and steam or boil till cooked.
Serve with chutney or a light tempering.

tipsList.title: Tip 1
tipsList.desc: Steamed rice-flour dumplings with spiced dal filling – light and nourishing.

tipsList.title: Tip 2
tipsList.desc: A traditional Bihari comfort dish.

title: Aloo Chokha
steps: Mash the boiled potatoes while warm. Mix with finely chopped onion, green chilli, raw mustard oil and salt.
Serve with litti, roti or as a side.

fullIngredients.name: Onion, green chilli, mustard oil, salt

tipsList.title: Tip 1
tipsList.desc: Simple, pungent mashed potato preparation – a staple side in Bihari meals.

tipsList.title: Tip 2
tipsList.desc: Raw mustard oil is the key flavouring.
